tool.name: TransVar annotations

param.name: sources
param.label: Transcript annotation sources
param.help: TransVar can consult several transcript sets at once. Every selected source is downloaded and can then be switched on individually in the TransVar tool.

param.name: refversion
param.label: Reference version
param.help: TransVar builds its coordinates against a specific genome assembly. The wrapper passes this value on as --refversion.

param.name: name
param.label: Display name
param.help: Leave empty to generate a name from the reference version and the selected sources.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Downloads the pre-built transcript annotation databases that TransVar_ needs and makes them available to the TransVar tool through the ``transvar_annotations`` data table.
Running ``transvar config --download_anno`` by hand writes the databases and TransVar's configuration file into the installed Python package directory. That directory is shared between jobs and usually read-only on a Galaxy server, so this data manager downloads the same files into a Galaxy managed data directory instead.
**Annotation sources**
Only annotation sets that are openly licensed and freely redistributable are offered:
============== =================================================== Source Provided by ============== =================================================== RefSeq NCBI, public domain CCDS NCBI/EBI consensus CDS, public domain Ensembl EMBL-EBI, free of restrictions GENCODE EMBL-EBI/WTSI, free of restrictions UCSC RefGene UCSC Genome Browser refGene table (RefSeq derived) UCSC knownGene UCSC Genome Browser knownGene table ============== ===================================================
AceView is *not* offered, because it is published for use with attribution but states no redistribution licence. The genome sequence and dbSNP downloads that TransVar also offers are not fetched either: Galaxy already manages reference genomes through the ``fasta_indexes`` data table, and the TransVar tool takes its reference genome from there.
Not every source exists for every assembly, so the list of sources changes with the selected reference version. TransVar also names mm9 as a supported assembly, but no pre-built databases are published for it, so it is not offered here.
**Download size**
Each source is a database file plus its indices, together roughly 10 MB (CCDS) to 70 MB (Ensembl, GENCODE). Selecting every source for one human assembly downloads in the order of 250 MB.
**Servers behind an HTTP proxy**
The download runs inside a Galaxy job, and Galaxy reduces a job's environment to ``HOME``, ``LC_CTYPE``, ``PATH`` and ``TMPDIR``. A proxy configured in the shell or in the Galaxy server's own environment therefore does not reach this tool, and the download fails with a connection timeout. Set it on the job destination instead, for example in ``job_conf.yml``::
execution: environments: local: runner: local env: - name: https_proxy value: ADDRESS-OF-YOUR-PROXY - name: http_proxy value: ADDRESS-OF-YOUR-PROXY
**Repeated runs**
Each combination of reference version and sources becomes one data table entry, so re-running with the same selection refreshes that entry rather than adding a duplicate.
.. _TransVar: https://bioinformatics.mdanderson.org/public-software/transvar/
